_meta.what: Registered domain-to-tier map for presentation ordering and the spike-quality metric. Tiers order the receipts drill-down credible-first and feed the tier 1-2 share shown on Why cards; they NEVER enter any score. Assignments cite documented behaviors (fabrication incidents, retraction practice), not viewpoints. Changes are append-only with a dated reason.

criteria.1: wire services and public-service international broadcasters with formal correction processes
criteria.2: national and international broadsheets and business press with mastheads and published corrections
criteria.3: mainstream TV, portals, and aggregating outlets with editorial staff but weaker correction records
criteria.4: outlets with documented fabrication incidents or syndication mills with no original reporting

_meta.tier4_note: Tier-4 assignments below stand on the registered criteria. Syndication-mill designations are verifiable from this project's own datapacks (identical wire copy across domains, no original reporting). Broadcast-outlet assignments are held as PROVISIONAL pending author-supplied citations to documented incidents (IFCN signatory fact-checks); until cited, those outlets rank tier 3 in presentation. No reason stated here makes a claim beyond the cited evidence.
_meta.international_note: International expansion 2026-08-04 per the founder and the FICCI director: global and regional outlets classified by the same criteria. State-CONTROLLED outlets (editorial line set by a government, an ownership fact) sit at tier 4 with that stated reason; state-FUNDED but editorially independent broadcasters (BBC, DW, France 24, Al Jazeera) are classified on their correction practices like anyone else.
